notes: Summary: Zengrit builds sub-100ms scoring and moderation for live multiplayer games. Extremely latency- and cost-sensitive; if inference budget spikes, they throttle features. Evaluation focused on reducing unit cost while keeping p50/p95 within tight SLOs.

Business context: onboarding 3 AAA titles for season launch Q3. Each title generates short prompts (~20 tokens) for moderation + user-intent signals for matchmaking. Peak concurrency expected: regional bursts up to ~1.5k concurrent inference requests (short responses). Cost targets: reduce per-session inference spend by 30-50% vs current hosted provider.
Technical targets (customer):
- Latency: p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 180ms for 8-32 token responses (end-to-end request->first-token).
- Throughput: sustain 400 RPS regional burst with graceful tail latency under autoscale policies.
- Cost: target $/k token reduction of 30% via quantization + smarter batching.
Current infra & constraints:
- Prototype uses mixed cloud GPUs; prefer Dedicated pool for predictability and co-location with game servers.
- Must support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. SOC2 compliance required by procurement.
Model preferences & routing:
- Primary: compact 7-13B open models; exploring 4-bit/8-bit quantized variants for throughput gains.

- Routing: low-latency regional routing with fallback to cheaper quantized variants during peak load. Want policy to prioritize p50 latency for matchmaking requests over non-critical moderation tasks.
Optimize interest (explicit asks):
- Batching: recommendations for per-route batch size limits and latency-aware batching to maximize GPU utilization without increasing p95 beyond targets.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated short-turn prompts (player session history). Need guidance on TTLs and cache warming for rolling player pools.
- Quantization: comparison of fp16 vs 8-bit vs 4-bit on our short-prompt workload; impact on hallucination rate for moderation tasks and token-cost savings.
Perf benchmarking POC plan (agreed on call 2026-03-01):
- Redwood to run 3-day perf suite on Dedicated pool configured with: 4x A10-style nodes (customer sim), adaptive batching enabled, prefix caching enabled for 2 routes (moderation, matchmaking).
- Synthetic traffic: ramp to 400 RPS steady-state with bursts to 1.5k for 10m windows each 2 hours; profile GPU utilization, p50/p95/p99, token/sec, and cost per million tokens metric.
- Variants: baseline fp16, 8-bit quantized, 4-bit quantized (if supported) + routing policy that falls back to 8-bit under >80% utilization.

- Success criteria: p50 <= 60ms in primary region on majority of windows, p95 <= 180ms on steady-state, cost reduction >= 30% vs baseline provider, and no >5% accuracy/regression in moderation classification (QA eval set).
